memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'When Pharaoh calls you in and asks, "What is your occupation?" you should answer, "Your servants have tended livestock from our boyhood on, just as our fathers did." Then you will be allowed to settle in the region of Goshen, for all shepherds are detestable to the Egyptians.'" — Gen 46:33-34 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joseph tells his brothers to say plainly what they are: shepherds. And he tells them why — because Egyptians despise shepherds, and that very fact will win them Goshen, a region apart, where they can live undisturbed and keep their identity intact.

What could have been a humiliation becomes a protection. If the Egyptians had admired them, Israel would have been absorbed into Egypt within a few generations and vanished. The rejection is precisely what preserves them as a distinct people.

God does that. Sometimes the very thing that makes you an outsider is the thing that keeps you.

Christians are told plainly that we should not be surprised when the world does not embrace us (Jn 15:19; 1 Pet 4:12). It is uncomfortable, and it is lonely at times. But it also keeps us from dissolving into a culture that would happily absorb us and leave nothing distinct behind.

Notice too that Joseph does not tell them to hide who they are or dress it up as something grander. Be honest about your occupation. There is a quiet dignity in that — no pretending, no shame, no apology.

And consider this: God later chose to call Himself the Shepherd of Israel, and Jesus called Himself the Good Shepherd (Jn 10:11). What Egypt detested, God took as His own name.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where does being a Christian make you an outsider?
2. Are you tempted to blend in rather than be honest about who you are?
3. How does it encourage you that Christ took the title of Shepherd?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, give me courage to be honest about who I am and whose I am, even when it costs me acceptance. Thank You that Jesus is my Good Shepherd. Amen.
